In his commentary on sakhi 30, revered Yadunath Maharaj writes about the phrase "jahan mage tahan det" — to those possessed of riddhi-siddhi, it gives wherever asked. You know the story of Lakshmichand Sheth of Vrindavan. He was a man favoured by Lakshmi. To test him, someone once devised a scheme. As he was being ferried across the river in a boat, in the middle of the river the man stopped the boat and demanded of Lakshmichand: I want money right now, this very moment — give it. Lakshmichand told him to wait until they reached the other bank, but the man would not agree and pressed insistently; then, scooping handfuls of river water, the water turned into coins, and thus, in the very middle of the river, as much money as he demanded was given to him. Even though he possessed such powers, Lakshmichand set aside riddhi-siddhi and came to Vrindavan to practise loving devotion. His temple is in Vrindavan. Thus, regarding riddhi-siddhi, Vyasji says in this sakhi:

_Vyas asht siddh nav nidh, rahi thari kar jor, pamar jiv mohe lagi rahe, mai kab nirakhu Nand Kishor ||52||_ (Vyasji says the eight siddhis and nine treasures stand with folded hands before God and say: base, weak-minded people cling to us, but we, the eight riddhis and nine nidhis, only long for the day we may have the good fortune of beholding Nandkishor Krishna. Loving devotees pay no heed to riddhi; they hold only to devotion.)

Jivanji Maharaj says: the riddhi-siddhi that is in you — we have no need of it; we are capable of giving whatever anyone needs, whenever they need it. In other words, Harijans have no need at all of riddhi-siddhi, for they have already surrendered everything to Krishna. They have only to worship Shri Hari. Moreover, the Sadguru has laid out their path for them; their provision has already come about merely by their placing faith in the Sadguru's words. So riddhi-siddhi always says: let the Harijans go on worshipping Hari, we shall place no obstacle in their way.

When Kabirji manifested in Kashi and set about uprooting ritual karmakand, the Vedic paths and the Vedas pleaded that they be allowed to go on living in the world, that their existence not be destroyed, and Veda, Purana, mantra-japa, tapa, yagna and the rest began to say: we possess a certain special quality — we are capable of bestowing riddhi and siddhi, and through us people receive whatever they wish for; but even if you should choose to disregard us, do so — we for our part will place no hindrance in your way, and if, without harbouring any illusion about us, you Hari-bhaktas wish to go on worshipping Hari at your ease, do so — this is what they always say. And they say: you may go on with your Hari-bhakti, but please do not banish us from the world altogether. ||30||

With Kabirji's coming, the clouds of ritual karmakand that had gathered over the path of devotion were cleared away, and full light was granted. Rejoicing began among the devotees, and, casting aside ritual, karmakand and religion-of-works, he made Raghuvir Shri Ram manifest. ||31||

The tangles and deceptions that lay within ritual and religion — leading one down to ruin through riddhi-siddhi and the rest — the Sadguru has shown us these, showing how the Veda had kept devotion hidden under the guise of ritual and religion. Our Sadguru has revealed to us the secret of Raghupati Shri Ram, whom karma, dharma and the Vedic scriptures had kept concealed, and he has let us behold devotion to Raghupati. ||32||

The Sadguru has shown us the truth-principle that was present in the three worlds, and the name of the supreme truth, Parbrahm, by which King Janak delivered thousands of souls suffering the torments of hell — that name, "Ram," he has shown us. ||33||

The thousand-hooded Sheshnag, through his thousand mouths, continuously chants that very name of Ram; by that name Hanuman made stones float upon the sea. Such a priceless name my Sadguru has given me — the same name that Gauripati Shankar Bhagwan too continuously chants and meditates upon. ||34||

I was caught up in ritual karmakand, pilgrimage, and vows; the Sadguru helped me and, to rescue me from this suffering, showed me the path of devotion through Ram's name. After that, devotion became very easy for me. Until then, having found no one to give me Ram's name through many births, I had clung to ritual karmakand, pilgrimage and vows, painful as a thorny babul tree.

My life has become blessed, for my Sadguru took hold of me with his own hand, gave me support, and showed me the true path. So devotion became easy for me. And not just now, but through many births, without finding anyone to give me the name of Ram, which is otherwise unobtainable, I had taken refuge in ritual, religion, pilgrimage and vows, harmful as a thorny babul tree. But now that the Sadguru has given me the name of Ram, I have been saved from this painful ritual religion. ||35||

After the Sadguru gave me the teaching of Ram's name, this birth of mine has now become the very last one. I no longer have to fall into the cycle of coming and going through the womb. Now, simply through keeping company with the sants, I have attained devotion to and the presence of Ram, the king of Ayodhya.

Jivanji Maharaj says: this is my last birth. Through my Sadguru's teaching, I shall no longer have to fall into the cycle of birth and death. In the company of sants I have attained the name and the presence of Ram, the king of Ayodhya. ||36||

Before the Sadguru's word, the eight kinds of siddhi and the nine treasures are of no use at all. My place is now in the sixteen-arted Parbrahm's own abode, where the servants and devotees of Shri Hari forever dwell. ||37||

He from whose lotus navel Brahma was born — that very Parbrahm Narayan himself grazed cows in Gokul; he on whose head shines the crown of peacock feathers, and around whose neck the garland of gunja-berries — Jivanji Maharaj has recognized him, and now nothing else is needed. He is Vrajraj, the protector of Vraj. ||38||

This dialogue-satsang took place in Samvat 1983, on the thirteenth of the bright half of Aso. What was set forth in it was this: the flute-charming Lord — this Brahma is called nirgun (without attributes), but the attribute lies concealed, held in reserve, within him. Together with the five elements and the three gunas, he gathers up all the senses within himself as if into a house, folding everything away. That is to say, whatever is seen in the manifest world is but the powerful shadow of the nirgun Brahma. Everything happens by his will and wish. The soul often acts against his will; then it becomes bound by the fetter of that action, falls into the bondage of karma, and every soul must undergo the fruit of that karma. Parbrahm is nirgun — the world knows this — yet Parbrahm keeps his quality of possessing attributes (sagun) held in reserve, apart, for this manifest world, and this is the cause of the relative, dependent world, which dwells within this attribute. All beings, subtle bodies and the whole universe rest upon that very nirgun Parbrahm — that is, the world of beings remains coiled around him. Yet, despite this, no being is able to know him; all beings and subtle forms, though separated from the one supreme principle, turn away from it on account of karma — so that, even while dwelling together with him, none of them understands the dharma of Vasudev. And so they fall into birth and death and the six schools of philosophy, and waste their human birth in vain; and some fall into hollow hypocrisy and undergo the eighty-four lakh species. To this, Baba Kabirji stands witness.

In the satsang, on the subject of the course of birth and death, a sakhi is given from Kabirji's "Svanaid" (Maya) section. "Sva" means: the devotee's arising in this world happens differently from that of other worldly people; how the soul is contained within the egg is explained in this section. So, to understand the sakhi about the course of birth and death, it will be better understood by first looking at the sakhi that precedes it, which is —

_Na ko id upare, na ko id heth, na ko id pakhale, jiv rahe ta madhya pet ||53||_ (Svaka Id) (Kabirji says that the egg through which the soul comes is not, outside the body, in the sky; nor is it below in the netherworld; nor does this egg exist under anyone's independent authority — rather, the soul lies contained, hidden, within the belly of that egg, unseen.)

_Janma marana gati bijame, jog bhog te mahi, puran parcho vishvakun, avar na alagun chahe ||54||_ (Svaka Id ||10||) (Kabirji says the condition of a soul's birth and death lies within the seed of the egg, and within the sexual union that a soul experiences its origin is contained. The entire universe, with its eighty-four lakh species, has had the full experience of this union, and no other soul can wish to be born by any means other than this.)

On the subject of yog and bhog, in the reserved (Anamat) section, Kabirji says —

_Kabir sukh dukh sampat vipat sab, so to karma sanjog, addishta jog un mahe nahi, so to ulato amirasa bhog ||55||_ (Anamat Ang) (Kabirji says that whatever pleasure, pain, prosperity or adversity a soul obtains in this world comes about through the combination of the fruits of karma; but the unseen grace of God that a devotee receives does not fall within this fruit of karma — this soul, who is a devotee, is, contrary to the world, one who drinks the nectar-sweet essence of devotion.)

Regarding the souls of the world and His own devotees, Kabirji says —

_Kabir gyan vichar aur nij bhagat, e addishta sanjog, riddhi siddhi sampat vipat, sab e karma phal bhog ||56||_ (Anamat Ang) (Kabirji says there is an unseen, subtle bond between knowledge, reflection and the devotee — that is, through the thought of the direct realization of Parbrahm's own manifest form, this unseeable connection binds them together. Whatever riddhi, siddhi, pleasure or pain a devotee receives — all this he understands as the fruit of karma being undergone.)

Further, the satsang says —

_Kabir antariksha idu agamko, adhar rahu niradhar, nitya vikase nirman phal, trigun vriksh vistar ||40||_ (Svanaid ||3||) (Kabirji says the egg of unfathomable Nature exists in space — in the great elements — suspended without any support, and it forever develops, spreading out into the tree of the world, bringing forth the fruit that constitutes the tree of the three gunas.)

_Kabir savalakh nirmanamen, uthai nitya avaj, lakh sabad samata samai, rahata anamit gaj ||41||_ (Kudarat ||22||) (Kabirji says that in the creation of the eighty-four lakh species, within this three-gunas creation of Aum, a sound is forever arising from the one-and-a-quarter-lakh word-sounds of Aum, such as the six schools of philosophy and the rest; but out of these, a lakh of these word-sounds fall silent, while the trigunatit — beyond the three gunas — "rankar," which is held in reserve, unceasing and unbroken, goes on resounding.)

In the composition of a pada titled Bhavtaran attributed to Kabirji, in a pada headed "Shabad," it says —

Shabad:

_Cheto re cheto nar bavare, kaha achet rahai, kal daga hai sir upare, sabkun dhar khai ||1||
Lachh jiv nit khat hai, sava lakh upai hau, kahukun chhode nahi, aise kal anyai hau ||2||
Jagat chabena hai kalko, sabko khat chugai hau, chun chun khaye shurma, khate na aghai hau ||3||
Kul marjada metke, karo tum sat sagai hau, kahe Kabir tab bench hau, kal daga mit jai hau ||4||_

(Kabirji says: O foolish man, awake — why do you go about senseless? Deceitful death circles above your head; it seizes and devours everyone. Every day it eats a lakh souls and creates another lakh and a quarter, but it lets no one go — such a deceiver is it. The whole world is death's morsel, its snack; it picks everyone out one by one and devours them; it has devoured even the great heroes, one by one, and even so is never sated. So give up the bonds of family custom and ritual and join yourself truly to the true name of God — only then, Kabir says, will you be saved, and the fear of death's deceit will vanish.)

In the satsang, two sakhis of the Bij (seed) section are given, stating —

_Kabir bund athah jalhar samudra, thak mag kachhu nahi, idu trisamen bhagame, sab jag upji vilay ||43||_ (Bij ||14||) (Kabirji says the drops of water surging in the fathomless ocean are endless — their extent cannot be measured. In the same way, from just the thirtieth part of Parbrahm's egg, this world is born and merges back into dissolution; and the measure of this universe cannot be found.)

_Kabir id trisama bhagaka, bhalka chhuta ek, tine tin lok mariya, varpar nahi chhek ||44||_ (Bij ||15||) (Kabirji says that from the thirtieth part of the whole Parbrahm, only a single fragment has broken free — by it alone he has brought all three worlds under his sway. He has drawn all three worlds into a whirl, and it cannot be fathomed to its very end.)

Just as a drop of water separates out from a fathomless ocean, so from God's egg the thirtieth part has separated out; from it this entire world has been produced, and in it — the thirtieth part — that same world again dissolves, that is, is absorbed back into it. Kabirji says that the cycle of birth and death happens again and again due to the fruit of one's karma, and, on the basis of that karma-fruit, the soul also undergoes yog and bhog; the soul who has once grown fond of sense-pleasure cannot understand the other path, the path of devotion. This original source of the world's creation, Parbrahm, is unfathomable, beyond knowing; and yet the world exists coiled around him. It is forever developing, and it also perishes — that is, such coming-and-going is happening in the world at every single moment. In this universe there are thousands and lakhs of those who know and understand Parbrahm, who continuously do namasmaran (remembrance of the Name); their voices sound without ceasing, and the resonance of the many merges into Him. In the end, only one truth remains — the name of Parbrahm. Kabirji says that in the ocean there are countless, abundant drops of water, having rained down as rain; they have obtained nothing through any effort of their own — in just the same way, from the thirtieth part of Parbrahm, this entire world has come to be formed, and into it, it dissolves again. From this egg — Parbrahm — the thirtieth part that separated out (Krishna), who sustains all three worlds — this universe rests upon that support. The bond between the soul, the world, and the Lord of the world, Parbrahm, is tied by one single thread. The soul is bound to undergo the fruit of its own karma. Hence the soul, without freedom, must undergo both sin and merit. Thus, according to the law of the universe, the soul undergoes the fruit of its karma. From this karma there is no way to gain liberation except by taking refuge in the Sadguru. Because —

_Evam sansaramananni jivanyahamaddashtavan, yatha karma tatha labha iti shastranidarshanam ||13||_ (Maha Shanti 279-20) (In this way I have seen all souls caught in the cycle of birth and death. Moreover, it is also the settled view of the scriptures that as is the karma, so is the fruit obtained.)

_Kshapayitva tu tam kalam ganitam kalachodita, savasheshena kalena sambhavanti puna: puna: ||14||_ (Maha Shanti 279-18) (Having exhausted, in heaven or hell, the reckoned time of enjoying the fruit of karma, then, through the remaining karma-experience, driven onward by time together with karma, the soul is born again and again into the world.) Because —

_Kalai sampurna siddhi:_ (Samagam, Shlok 1) and _Kala: srijati bhutani_ (Samagam, Shlok 2) — in this way the entire world is subject to time. Through virtuous deeds, heaven is attained, and through sinful deeds, hell.

_Nashe'yam satatam dehi nripate punyapapayo:, tata eva samutthena tamasa rudhyate'pi cha ||15||_ (O king, the soul is not free in the matter of undergoing the fruits — pleasure and pain — of virtue and sin. It, the soul, becomes veiled by the darkness born of these very virtues and sins.)

In the Mahabharata there is a highly telling dialogue on the subject of karma between a Brahmin and a vaishya named Jajali. The vaishya Jajali explains to a Brahmin what his true karma really is. Whatever deeds are done out of desire for heaven and the like — once the soul has enjoyed their fruit and returns from there, it invites its own ruin.

_Sa eva subhago bhutva punarbhavati durbhaga:, vyapattim karmanam drishtva jugupsanti jana: sada ||16||_ (Maha Shanti 262-34) (Having enjoyed that heaven, the soul again falls under the sway of misfortune. Seeing this destruction that overtakes actions, the righteous always condemn actions done with desire.)

Because one who performs desire-driven action performs religious acts along with attachment. He who performs the Jyotishtom or Agnishtom sacrifice out of desire for heaven, or performs sacrifice to obtain a son or wealth, undergoes the fruit of that karma. Hence, if karma is not renounced before death, then even after death, though the body is no more, that karma does not perish — rather, it remains together with the soul, and the soul does not attain Parbrahm. Therefore the soul must renounce both sin and merit. Among all this, what is the essential truth? Shri Krishna tells Arjuna —

_Nirvanam paramam brahma dharmo'sau para uchyate, tasmanna chyutapurvo'hamachyutastena karmana ||17||_ (Maha Shanti 342-81) (That which is the supreme nirvana, the state of peace, Parbrahm — that alone is dharma. I have never before fallen from that state; therefore I am called Achyut, the unfallen.)

Thus, Narayan Parbrahm alone is worthy of remembrance, and it is by Him that all karma is destroyed and the supreme state may be reached.

_Harireva hi kshetragyo nirmamo nishkalastatha, jivashcha sarvabhuteshu panchabhutagunatiga: ||18||_ (348-58) (Bhagwan Shri Hari alone is the Kshetragya, the Knower of the field; he is free of possessiveness and without division; he alone, present in all beings, dwells as the soul, transcending the qualities of the five elements.) Because —

In the satsang, in Kabirji's Dedar Ang sakhi, it says —

_Kabir sab ghat bhitar sal gaman, asan adya madya anta, sikhe san jagatki, asan bhaya sab sant ||56||_ (Dedar ||42||) (Kabirji says that in every single body born into this world, Parbrahm's radiance — sal, water — moves through beginning, middle, and up to the very end; so anyone in this world who learns this hint of the mystery, the hint of God who moves in this way, and thereafter refuses to bind himself to the web of the world's maya — that is, is not willing to accept being ensnared by maya — such a person, all of them, are called sants.)

_Kabir asan bhaya ati, akala bol bandh bhav pas, chhutanko upay kahu, jo rahai ekamana vishvas ||57||_ (Dedar ||43||) (Kabirji says that sants who become extremely impatient not to be caught in the world's web of maya — even though the mind, lured by maya, may urge them toward the bond of worldly attachment — those who, in their eagerness to be free of that bondage, refuse to go toward maya, to them I show the means of release: if they keep firm-minded faith and remain untouched by maya, they will be freed from the bond of the world.)

Further, at the end of the Dedar Ang, it says —

_Kabir hun tu tehavun jab hua, tab miliya Maharaj, dilki dubadha mit gai, tab sahaj sarai sab kaj ||58||_ (Dedar ||44||) (Kabirji says when the realization came that "I and You are one," then God was met, and the mind's worries and doubts vanished; then, with natural ease, the task of attaining the vision of God's form was accomplished.)

God, who is nirgun, moves through the water of the ocean of existence from the very beginning to the very end, and pervades everywhere in the world; that God is attained by the sant who remains untouched by maya. In the satsang, finally, in Kabir's Anamat Ang sakhi, it says —

_Kabir sujh vinako sal gaman, ghat ghat raho samay, age kachhu sujhai nahi, utapat pralai jay ||45||_ (Anamat ||64||) (Kabirji says God is contained within every single body — ghat. Without the discernment and understanding by which He can be glimpsed through remaining free of sense-vices, the soul must move through the ocean of existence. Because of attachment to sense-pleasures, nothing else is visible to it, and so it must wander in the arising and dissolving of birth and death.)

One who has come to true understanding through the words of the Sadguru need not fall into the cycle of birth and death. Kabir has said —

_Ek samana sakalmen sakal samana tahi, Kabir samana bujhmen, tahan dusara nahi ||59||_ (Bijak 266) (The one Parbrahm is contained within all beings; but Kabirji says, through my true understanding, I have come to understand Ram, the indweller who shines throughout the universe, contained within the world — He is contained in that understanding, and I have come to see Parbrahm alone everywhere; no longer looking at anything else, I have become a free devotee, His servant.)

Kabirji says that Parbrahm is contained within, and dwells in, all beings. Yet, under the sway of time, one forgets that Parbrahm. Even so, in the beginning, middle, and final states, if the soul, becoming free of karma, can recognize Parbrahm, it can go to Parbrahm's abode; but if it goes on following the ways of the world, then the cycle of birth and death continues without end; yet if it has kept the company of sants, it can cross over the ocean of existence.

Parbrahm dwells in every single body, but without the company of the Sadguru, the discernment does not come, and so no path ahead is visible, and the soul remains stuck in this ocean of existence.

For this, they have called Kabirji the Lord of the world and the universe. That is to say, those beings who are under the sway of maya — their worship, and their notion of God, regarding the deity they follow as God, is a separate matter from the worship of the sants and Parbrahm's own devotees, whose devotion is unattached and free of the world. Jivanji Maharaj says that those whose god is Shiva, Brahma, and the like — even they exist within the eighty-four lakh species; so those who remain within these eighty-four lakh species and follow deity-worship, vows and the like — even though Parbrahm pervades and dwells within every single body, they are unable to touch Him. In the end, their servants and worshippers do not attain liberation from the eighty-four lakh species, and they must wander here and there in the world. But whoever seeks out the true Sadguru and takes refuge with him need have no worry at all, because he becomes free of desire and devotes himself wholly to devotion. So he no longer has any other fear, because —

_Maranako dar Hari nam bin, dise sab sansar, harijan ugare jivana, so Sadguruke upkar ||60||_ (In the world, whoever is without the name of Parbrahm lives in fear of death. But by the Sadguru's grace, the Harijan crosses this ocean of existence with the support of the "Name" — he alone is truly fearless.) Because —

_Nirbhay khat Kabirki, sab santan lini bant, take kachhu nahi jivana, jake man men ant ||61||_ (All of us have Kabirji as our Sadguru, and his presence is fearless. So all sants and devotees have accepted Kabirji's name. But for those whose minds are still caught up in the world's maya, and in whose minds there is still confusion and doubt — for such souls, Jivanji Maharaj says he has nothing more to say, because they are bound to drown and perish in the ocean of existence.)

In the satsang, in the chapter on Mayabrahma's Bhel, the first two lines quoted are from a pada by Kabirji. The next two lines of this same pada, "Panch tatva trigun shakat kari saniya," are given at the end of this chapter, "Vachan Ej Parmeshwar" —

_Akarki ot akar nahi ubare, Shiv Virinchi Vishnu ja tanhi, jasaka sevak tas, bhal bhavahi, ishtakun chhod age na jai ||46||_ (Kabirji says: if one form remains sheltered under the cover of another form, then when that sheltering form perishes, the form dependent on it cannot survive either. In this matter, even great gods like Shiva, Brahma, or Vishnu — when, at the dissolution of this creation, these three great gods themselves also perish, then the devotees who took refuge in those gods also perish along with them. So whoever is a devoted servant, worshipping and adoring some deity, merges into that deity's own refuge, and cannot go forward, leaving his chosen deity behind, to take shelter with one who stands even higher than that deity.)

Namdev has written a pada about the fate that befalls whoever worships whatever deity —

_Na taris na taris Ram bina,
jap le ho jivda tu Ram nam ||teka||
jaldev pujila to kachla hoyla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||1||
Chandi pujila to mrigla hoyla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||2||
Devi pujila to bhensa hoyla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||3||
Harsadi pujila to rudhir piyela,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||4||
Khetrapal pujila to kukra hoyla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||5||
Ganesa pujila to musa hoyla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||6||
Mahadev pujila to vrishabh hoyla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||7||
Suraj pujila to ashva hoyla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||8||
Sannyasi pujila to Shivlok jayla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||9||
Brahman pujila to sargalok jayla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||10||
Bhagat pujila to bhagta hoyla,
janam janam Namdev nishan bajayla ||1||_

(Namdevji says: O soul, you will not cross over without Ram, so chant the name of Ram. If you worship the water-god, you will become a wave, a crab — devotion will not come about without Ram. If you worship Chandi, you will become a deer, an animal; worship Devi, you will become a buffalo; worship Harshad Mata, you will have to drink blood — note: when the messengers of Yama lead a sinful soul to hell, and that thirsty soul, tormented by the sun's heat, begs for water, Harshad Mata, seated at a water-stall along the way, gives exactly as much water as the amount of blood she receives; since this Harshad Mata is blood-thirsty, she can only give her worshipper blood in return. Worship Kshetrapal, you will have to become a dog. Worship Ganpati, you will have to become a mouse. Worship Mahadev, you will have to become a bull, an ox. Worship Surya, you will have to become a horse. Serve a sannyasi, you will go to Shivlok; worship Brahma, you will go to Swarglok. But if you worship a devotee (bhagat), you too will become a devotee, and you will remain a devotee birth after birth — this proclamation Namdev has sounded and spread abroad.)

Vyasji too has composed a pada of this same sentiment (Raag Ramkali) —

_Jaki upasana tahiki vasana, tahiko namrup gun gaiyai,
yahai ananya dharma paripati, Vrindavan basi anat na jaiyai ||teka||
soi bibhachari an kahai an karai takau mukh dekhen darun dukh paiyai,
Vyas hoi upahas tras kiyai, as achhat kit das kahaiyai ||2||_

(Vyasji says: whatever deity one worships, one carries within oneself a longing for that deity, and one ought to sing the name, form and praises of that same deity — this is the way of exclusive devotion, fixed on one alone: so that one who dwells in Vrindavan ought not to go anywhere else. But if such a person says one thing and does another, then he is to be counted an adulterer in devotion; even to look upon his face brings terrible suffering. So Vyasji says: if, while posing as the worshipper of one's chosen deity, a person disregards and mocks that deity, tyrannizing it, then even the slight hope he might have of being called that deity's devotee is itself found wanting — so how then could he be called that deity's devotee?)

In the Bijak, Kabir has spoken this sakhi —

_Bhakti bhakti sabkoi kahai, bhakti na ai kaj, jahanko kiya bharosava, tahante ai gaj ||62||_ (Everyone goes about saying "devotion, devotion," and performs devotion to various deities, but that devotion proved useless in the end — whatever deity one placed one's trust in gave assurance for a while, and all of them were of the nature of time; time carried its worshippers off into its own realm — but when the great dissolution came, both the chosen deity and its worshipper perished, and when the world was created anew, both were born again according to their karma.)

(Explaining "Akarki Ot," revered Yadunath Maharaj writes: "behind a form that has hands and feet, another form cannot survive.") In the Gita, chapter 7, verses 22-23, it says —

_Sa tatha shraddhaya yuktastasyaradhanamihate, labhate cha tata: kamanmayaiva vihitanhi tan ||19||
Antavattu phalam teshan tadbhavatyalpamedhasam,
devandevayajo yanti madbhakta yanti mamapi ||20||_

Meaning: He, endowed with that faith, worships that deity, and through that deity, I myself...

...continued from the meaning of the previous verse... "the desired enjoyments they themselves have created." ||22||

Meaning: But the fruit gained by those of little intelligence is perishable — those who worship the gods attain the gods, but My devotees attain Me. Whoever worships a particular deity becomes that deity's vehicle (vahana); regarding this it is said:

_Yasya devasya yadrupam tatha bhushanavahanam, tadrupa eva tacchaktir asuran yoddhum abhyayau. ||21||_
(Whatever form, ornaments, and vehicle belong to a given deity, that same deity's own power (shakti) arose in that very form to do battle with the demons.)

Swami Vivekanandaji has said in one place:

The various forms of worship of the gods (devatas) are all part of ritualistic religion (karmakand). Through them the worshipper certainly gets help in obtaining various kinds of divine enjoyments, but through them neither devotion (bhakti) nor liberation (mukti) can be attained. For this reason the Vedas have condemned worshippers of other deities, calling them ignorant; in some places they are even called animals:

_Atha yo'nyam devatam upaste anyo'sav anyo'ham asmiti na sa veda yatha pashuh._
(He who worships another deity, thinking "he is one and I am another," does not know the truth — he is like an animal.)

And in the Gita they are called of little intelligence.

One who takes shelter under the shade of a mere form (akar) — if instead he takes shelter under Parbrahm, he can be saved; regarding this it is said:

_Koi koi jogi bach gaye, Parbrahmaki ot,
Chakki chalti kaalki, padi sabhi par chot. ||63||_
(Some yogis, and only some, escaped by taking shelter in Parbrahm; the mill of Time keeps turning, and its blow falls on everyone else.)

Meaning: Those few yogis who took shelter in Parbrahm Parmatma were saved from the fear of Time (Kaal); everyone else has been struck by the ever-turning mill of Time. Kabirji says that other deities keep us away from devotion to Vishnu, keeping us apart from God.

_Kabir mai mashani shethi, Shitala Bheru bhoot Hanumant,
Sahebsu nyara rahai, jo inko poojant. ||64||_
(Kabir says: the Mother goddesses, the cremation-ground attendant-deities, Shitala, Bhairav, ghosts, Hanuman — whoever worships these remains separated from the Lord.)

Meaning: If one worships and serves the Mother goddesses, the cremation-ground attendant-deities, Shitala, Bhairav, ghosts, Hanuman, and other tamasic deities and demigods, they keep him away from devotion to God.

For this reason, creation is of two kinds: one is the mental creation (mansi srishti), the other is the sexual/procreative creation (maithuni srishti).

_Omkarse upno, Jivan jug sansar,
Rarankarse upno, so Sadguruko parivar. ||47||_
(From Omkar arose, O Jivan, the age-bound world; from Rarankar arose the true Guru's own family.)

_Omkarmaan aatle, sur Brahma munidev,
Rarankarmaan Jivana, je laga Sadguru sev. ||48||_
(Within Omkar wander, caught, the gods, Brahma, and sage-deities; within Rarankar, O Jivan, are those who have taken to the true Guru's service.)

_Akshar akshar ek Jivana, Omkarki aad,
Mamase raro bado, so Sadguru kahyo vichar. ||49||_
(Of all the letters, O Jivan, Om is the foremost; but "Ra" is greater than "Ma" — this is the teaching the true Guru has declared.)

_Ek aksharthi Jivana, bhayo brahmand vistar,
Raro rakhyo Harijana, mamo bhayo sansar. ||50||_
(From a single letter, O Jivan, the vast universe expanded; "Ra" is reserved for God's own people, "Ma" became the world.)

_E khare pade nahi Jivana, akal avinashi roop,
So gau charave Nandki, je Dashrath kul badbhoop. ||51||_
(This, O Jivan, never perishes — it is the imperishable, incomprehensible form; that same one grazes Nanda's cows, and is the great king of Dashrath's lineage.)

_Khare pade nahi Jivana, adbad ek aroop,
Utpat pralo jahaan jai same, so Sitapatiko roop. ||52||_
(It never perishes, O Jivan — it is one wondrous, formless being; where creation and dissolution both merge and rest, that is the form of Sitapati, the Lord of Sita.)

Jivanji Maharaj says that from the Omkar Pranav mantra arose the living creation under the sway of Maya — the mass of beings caught in the cycle of birth and death. But separate from this world born of Omkar, from the sound of Rarankar arose, free from the three gunas and desire-bound action, the true Guru's family — in the form of a reflection of Parbrahm — that is, the individual souls (jivatmas) who recognize Parbrahm. ||47||

_Rarankarku kahat hai, Brahma sarupi Ram,
Santdas tihu lokmein, sabahi iska kaam. ||65||_
(Rarankar, it is said, is Ram, of the very form of Brahm; O Santdas, in all three worlds, everything is His doing.)

"Ram," who is Parbrahm in form and beyond even Brahm, and by whose direction the activity of all three worlds proceeds — by His will alone all beings act. Here, under His shelter, the members of the true Guru's family, the disciples, have arisen from Rarankar, and it is into Him alone that they are to merge.

Within Omkar, which governs creation, sustenance, and dissolution, pundits, Brahma, sages, and gods keep colliding and wandering, being swept again and again through the stream of birth and death in this universe. But those who, remaining in the shelter of the true Guru, practise devotion and worship without desire — their place is established at the feet of Shri Ram, who is Parbrahm in form. ||48||

Jivanji Maharaj says that those who take refuge in Omkar have been deluded. This is because, among the words of the alphabet used to address the Lord Parbrahm, both the word "Om" and the letter "Ra" of the word "Ram" (which is Parbrahm's own form) occur. Because the word Om grants worldly action, karma, and its fruits, ordinary people of dull understanding are drawn more strongly toward it; and since the word Om has an attractive, decorative quality, the soul is pulled toward it the way a moth is pulled toward a flame. The letter "Ra," on the other hand, is not a word that has been specially embellished or falsely publicized in order to bring about attainment of the pure form of Parbrahm — it remains confined to true devotees alone. Thus, more than "A-U-M," the letter "Ra" in the word "Ram" is the finest and best of the entire alphabet, because by the utterance of its sound one attains Parbrahm. This is what the true Guru, having understood it, has declared. ||49||

From the single word of the imperishable, spotless, formless Parbrahm — who never perishes — this creation was formed, like an egg (anda). Among all beings in this universe, devotees who know this secret and are resolved to remain ever absorbed in devotion to Narayan have accepted and adopted the chanting of Rarankar as their constant remembrance. All other beings besides these devotees of God (Harijans) have accepted the word "Om," which ends in the letter "Ma," and so have fallen into the cycle of birth and death. ||50||

Jivanji Maharaj says that the name of Parbrahm is imperishable (akshaya) — that is, it does not decay or perish; moreover it is unaging and immortal, it does not fall or fade, meaning it does not perish; it is indestructible and incomprehensible. This same form of Parbrahm grazes King Nanda's cows in Gokul, and is the great King of Vraj who illumines the lineage of Dashrath. ||51||

He continues further, saying that the account of this imperishable, immortal form is wondrous — one of dull understanding cannot grasp it. Moreover, it is the form of Sitapati, the Lord of Sita, in whom creation and dissolution both merge, and He alone is Parbrahm. ||52||

With Rarankar in view, Rohidas composed this hymn (pad) in the Godi raga:

Godi:

_Jab ham Ram Ram, kahi gavega,
Rarankar hai tahai soi, taso antarmai milavega. ||Teka||
Loha samdrashta kanchan samdrashta, vish amrit sang dhavega,
Surnar muni durlabh pad, sohi tere avega. ||1||
Guru parsad bhai anbhe mat, bhed abhed milavega,
Kahe Rohidas meri aapa par, tab wa thade pavega. ||2||_
(When we sing "Ram, Ram," that very Rarankar dwelling within will unite our heart with Himself; iron and gold will seem the same to us, and worldly poison will run instead toward nectar; the state hard even for gods, men, and sages to attain will come to you. By the Guru's grace the mind becomes fearless, and the distinction between "different" and "non-different" dissolves; Rohidas says, when I stand beyond my own self, then He will be found standing right before me.)

Meaning: Rohidasji says that when we perform bhajan by chanting "Ram, Ram," that name of Ram will unite our inner self with God, who dwells there in the form of Rarankar. Then, whether it be iron or gold, we shall look upon both with equal vision (samdrishti), and even the poison-like objects of this world will begin to run toward the nectar-essence of Ram. Moreover, that state which is hard to attain even for gods, men, and sages will come to us. By the Guru's grace our mind will become fearless, and it will bring about union with the manifest form of God who lies hidden, concealed within this triple-natured (trigunī) creation. Rohidas says that when such ego (ahankar) is thus removed from within us, we shall find the essence of God standing directly before us.

It is said in the Samagam that taking shelter under a mere form does not save one who himself has form — meaning that whoever takes refuge in a god or goddess can receive only as much protection as that deity's own power allows. Therefore, of the creation that God has made in this world, it is fashioned in two ways: the first is the mental creation (mansi srishti), and the second is the sexual/procreative creation (maithuni srishti). The learned have also stated it as two kinds: the first, the creation of living beings (jiva srishti), and the second, the creation of the Lord (Ishwar srishti) — thus two kinds of creation have been described.

According to the principles of the Nyaya school regarding the soul (atma), fourteen qualities are attributed to the soul in its embodied (jiva) form: (1) pleasure, (2) pain, (3) ignorance, (4) desire, (5) aversion, (6) effort, (7) righteousness (dharma), (8) unrighteousness (adharma), (9) latent impressions of knowledge (sanskara), (10) number, (11) modification, (12) distinctness, (13) conjunction, and (14) disjunction.

It is said that God has manifested four kinds of creation:
1. The divine or godly creation (daivi, or sursampatti).
2. The demonic creation, or the creation of the flow (asuri srishti, or pravah srishti) — in the Bhagavad Gita, Lord Krishna tells Arjuna that there are only two kinds of creation; of these, the first is called the divine creation, and it has two further divisions, giving:
3. Maryada srishti — manifested by Brahma through the mind, in which beings such as Sanaka and his brothers, and Narada, appeared.
4. Pushti srishti — created from God's own limb, this is the creation that depends upon the path of Krishna's grace (kripanugraha). Whoever takes refuge in whichever kind of creation (form) has safety only for as long as that creation exists. The Gita, chapter 9, says:

_Te tam bhuktva swargalokam vishalam, kshine punye martyalokam vishanti,
Evam trayidharmam anuprapanna gatagatam kaamkaama labhante. ||21||_
(Having enjoyed that vast heaven, when their merit is exhausted, they attain the world of mortals; thus those who take shelter in the desire-driven path of Vedic religion, and who desire sense objects, undergo repeated coming and going.)

Activity proceeds within these two kinds of creation, that of Omkar and that of Rarankar. Within Omkar falls the creation bound by the three gunas, while Rarankar is a fourth state that transcends the three gunas. This devotion to Rarankar is practised only by the true followers of the true Guru; the Vedas and Puranas, on the other hand, proceed in accordance with the principle of Omkar. Therefore Jivanji Maharaj says:

_Pothi Parbrahm naamki, Sadgurue diya bataay,
Aadya avinashi Jivana, Ra re Ma me chit laay. ||66|| (Gurudev)_
(The true Guru has revealed the scripture of Parbrahm's name; O Jivan, fix your mind on the primordial, imperishable — on "Ra" and "Ma.")

Meaning: The four Vedas, the six Shastras, the eighteen Puranas, and many other such texts and scriptures exist, but the true Guru has revealed the scripture — the secret key — that shows genuine devotion in the shortest possible form, in which the mystery of the Supreme Truth is contained: the name of God. In this name dwells the primordial and imperishable Supreme Being, resting on only two letters, "Ra" and "Ma." Keep your attention fixed only on this name of Ram.

_Kabir padhvo dur kar, aru pustak de bahaay,
Pachaas akshar parhari, tu Ra re Ma me chit laay. ||67|| (Sar ka Ang)_
(Kabir says: give up studying, and cast away your books; abandon fifty letters, and fix your mind on "Ra" and "Ma.")

Meaning: Give up reading and studying scriptures and texts, set aside those books, and abandon fifty of the fifty-two letters as well; fix your attention on devotion and remembrance of God using only the two letters "Ra" and "Ma" within the name Ram.

Jivanji Maharaj goes even further than this.

_Bavan aksharmaan Jivana, ek akshar tatvasaar,
Ma maa pahelo je likhyo, teno Ved na pave paar. ||68|| (Prabodh)_
(Among the fifty-two letters, O Jivan, one letter is the essence of the truth: the one written before "Ma" — even the Vedas cannot fathom it.)

Meaning: Among the fifty-two letters of the alphabet, only one letter is especially important, and that is the letter in the name Ram which comes before "Ma" — that is, "Ra." Even the Vedas cannot fathom its mystery.

Kabirji says:

_Kabir akshar bolte, Omkar anusaar,
Aakarke bekaarko, moodh kahe Kirtaar. ||69||_
(Kabir says: one who merely utters the syllable in accordance with Omkar — the useless thing bound to mere form — the fool calls that the Creator.)

Meaning: One who follows and worships Omkar keeps repeating the syllable "Om, Om," but foolish, dull-witted people call this useless, three-gunas-bound Omkar the Supreme Being itself.

Here, Jivanji Maharaj has thus set forth the true form of Parbrahm. He has also shown Parbrahm as the Lord of the entire universe, and as the Lord of the devotees of Shri Hari's own dear ones (nija jan). Further, he has shown the division and multiplication of the gunas. At this point, a doubt arises on the opposing side (purvapaksha): if the universe worships "Omkar," why does Jivanji Maharaj speak of "Rarankar"? Let us first understand the matter of Omkar.

_Om ityetad aksharam idam sarvam, tasyopavyakhyanam bhutam bhavad bhavishyad iti sarvam omkara eva, yad anyat trikalatitam tad api omkara eva. ||23|| (Mandukya 1-1-1)_
(The syllable Om alone is everything; it is the explanation of whatever was, is, and will be. Therefore, whatever exists is Omkar alone; and whatever else exists beyond the three times — past, present, future — that too is Omkar alone.)

_Esha sarveshvara esha sarvajnah, esho'ntaryamy esha yonih sarvasya, prabhavapyayau hi bhutanam. ||24|| (Mandukya 1-1-6)_
(He is the Lord of all, He is omniscient, He is the indweller, and because He is the source of the origin and dissolution of all beings, He alone is the cause of everything.)

Furthermore, the Taittiriya Upanishad says:

_Om iti Brahma, Om itidam sarvam, Om ityetad anukritir hasma vaa apyashravayantyashravayanti, Om iti samani gayanti, Om shom iti shastrani shamsanti, Om ityadhvaryuh pratigaram pratigrinati, Om iti Brahma prasauti, Om ityagnihotram anujanati, Om iti Brahmanah pravakshyannaha brahmopapnavaniti. (Tai. 1-8-1)_
(The word Om is Brahman, for Om is all forms; Om is repetition. Saying "O Shravaya," one is made to listen with Om. Saying Om, the Sama hymns are sung — the chanting of the Samaveda. Saying Om, the sacred verses are recited. The adhvaryu priest utters Om after every ritual act. Saying Om, Brahma, the presiding deity of the Atharvaveda, grants permission. Saying Om, Agni consents to the performance of the sacrifice. Saying Om, a Brahmin who has not studied the Vedas nevertheless begins with Om. Saying Om, one expresses the wish, "May I attain Parbrahm.")

Resolution (Samadhan): We accept that all beings begin their worldly activity by first uttering the word "Om." And we have already said that the creation which arose from Omkar belongs to the path of desire-bound action (sakam karma). Those who perform the Vedic rites of yajna and sacrifice do so hoping for the fruit of their actions; and desire-bound action can never be without purpose — behind every action lies a definite result, and the soul must experience the good or bad fruit gained from that action. Furthermore, when the scripture (shruti) says that Om is omniscient and is the form of Parbrahm, that is not correct, because those who know only Omkar have stopped right there — they have not been able to go further, nor have they gained the capacity to understand the creation that lies beyond it. Their understanding is therefore like that of a frog in a well. Those who remain absorbed and content within the creation of Omkar experience only creation and dissolution — for they will never emerge from the whirlpool of birth and death, again and again. Regarding such souls, Kabirji says:

_Jhoothe sukhku sukh kahe, kachhu manat hai man mod,
E jagat chaveno kalko, kachhu mukhmein kachhu god. ||70||_
(He calls false happiness true happiness, and his mind takes some delight in it; this world is Time's own deceit — something in the mouth, something else hidden in the lap.)

This is because the fruit of action obtained through the worship of Omkar and the like, and the happiness gained by it, are merely a fleeting rush of feeling — not true happiness. Therefore Kabirji, giving a warning, says:

_Omkar nishre bhaya, so karta mati jaan,
Saacha shabd Kabirka, parde maanhi pichhaan. ||71|| (Sumiran-24)_
(Do not take the settled Omkar to be the Doer; recognize Kabir's true word hidden within the veil.)

To one who, by sounding the word Om, feels a certain sense of happiness, Kabirji says this is not the truth, so do not be misled by it. Kabirji has shown the true word. Do not take the settled, fixed Omkar to be the true Doer; instead, understand and reflect upon Ram, who dwells hidden within the body — behind the veil — the body made of the five elements. For —

_Jivroopyak antarbaasa, antarjyotiki naa pargaasa. ||2||_
(The soul dwells within, one in the form of the individual jiva; the inner light does not become manifest.)

We have already said that the individual soul (jiva), in the form of the collective (samashti), has taken up residence within the body; its awareness (surata) is something distinct. Though dwelling in this world, it remains untouched by it. What is called the "inner light" (antar jyoti) is the light of Parbrahm's own realm, which, by awakening awareness within the conscious soul, gives rise to the mind and its impressions (sanskaras), and thereby the soul becomes worldly, entangled in this world. If, in this state, one forgets Parbrahm, there remains the danger of turning onto the path of untruth. If the soul remains caught in delusion, it goes astray and misses the experience of the inner light. Today, because of external attractions in the world, the words of the true Guru cannot be understood, and so the soul loses its way. When the essence of the soul mistakes external light for Brahman, it falls into delusion. Therefore it must seek out the true path. If the meaning of the name "Ram," as explained by the true Guru, is neither known nor understood, then the soul, taking merely a worldly meaning, turns from its collective (samashti) form into an individual (vyashti) form. And this very process today, of turning from the collective form into the individual form, is itself the illusion (maya) in the form of the Gayatri. Just as the pure soul, by considering itself Brahman, has become impure — some regard it as the cause of the world, others regard it as the material cause — yet that so-called pure form of Brahman, even while called pure, is not pure; it is impure, that is, false (mithya). This is because those who belong to God (bhagwatjan) are free from all desires and from the world, as we have already established earlier. Whereas Omkar is bound by desire; the shruti (scripture) says:

_Tadetanmithunamomityaitasminnakshare sansrijyate yada vai,
Mithunau samagachchhata aapayata vai tavanyobhyasya kaamam. ||25||_
(This union is joined together by the syllable "Om." At the time when the pair come together, each obtains fulfilment of the other's desires — that is, "Om" is thereby proven to possess the quality of granting the fulfilment of all desires.)

Furthermore, the original teacher of the world, Shankaracharya, says:

_Yatha loke mithunau mithunavayavau stri punsau yada samagachchhato... gunvatvam omkarasya siddham ityabhiprayah... (Cha. 1-1-6)_
(Just as in the world a pair — a man and a woman as the members of the pair — come together, uniting through the ordinary act, and at that time fulfil each other's desires, so likewise, through this indwelling union, it is established that Omkar possesses the quality of granting the fulfilment of all desires.)

Here, commenting on the Chandogya Upanishad, it is stated that just as in the world a pair (mithuna) — that is, a man and a woman as the members of the pair — come together, uniting through the ordinary act of intercourse, and at that time fulfil each other's desires, in the same manner, through this indwelling union, it is established that Omkar possesses the quality of granting the fulfilment of all desires. This is our view.

Further, it is stated in a later section that the wise one (meaning the worshipper) who worships the syllable of the Udgitha word (the syllable chanted by the priest called Udgata) becomes one who brings about the fulfilment of all desires.

That is, such a Brahmin becomes capable of fulfilling even the complete desires of his patron (yajman) — that is, that Brahmin himself becomes subject to karma; and moreover, the patron for whom the mantras and rites are performed also, without fail, becomes bound to enjoy the fruits of that karma. It is further stated there that —

_Taddha etadanusaaksharam yadi kim chatujanatyo mityeva tadaha esha eva samriddhir yadanujna, samdharyata ha vai kamanam bhavati ya etadevam vidwan aksharam udgitham upaste. ||8||_
(Om itself is the syllable of consent; whenever anyone grants permission for anything, he says "Om." This granting of consent is itself abundance. If a person who knows this in this way worships the syllable Udgitha, he attains abundance of desires — he certainly attains the complete abundance of all his desires.)

For this very reason Jivanji Maharaj said to Krishnadas —

_Jot swaroop teenku thaharaya, Aadya Purush kinahu nahi paya,
Khat darshan tabhi upaye, Omkarku sabahi dhyaye. ||72||_
(They have taken the form of light to be the ultimate three; none has attained the Primordial Being; the six schools of philosophy arose only then, and all of them meditate upon Omkar.)

Thus, by declaring Omkar itself to be the form of divine light, the whole world has fallen into delusion, and cannot understand who the Primordial Being (Adya Purush) truly is; instead, people become absorbed in the worship of other deities, so that their lives are wasted in vain. Moreover, the fear of birth and death does not leave them — it does not spare even the gods. The deities whom human beings worship, considering them immortal, are themselves not immortal; when their merit (punya karma) is exhausted, they too must take birth again, and they too live in fear of death, because —

_Tanu tatra mrityuryatha matsyamudake paripashyedevam paryapashyadayi saamni yajushi,
Te nu viditvordhwa richah saamno yajushah swaram eva pravishan. ||26||_
("Just as a fisherman spots fish in the water, in the same way Death spotted these deities engaged in the rites connected with the Rig, Sama, and Yajur Vedas. Having come to know this, the deities withdrew from the rites connected with the Rig, Sama, and Yajur, and entered into pure sound.")

That is, just as fish become trapped in a fisherman's net and meet death, in the same way all beings — gods, gandharvas, kinnaras, human beings, and others of the maithuni (procreative) creation — become caught in death because of the fruits of their actions; that is, the fear of birth, old age, and death remains with them constantly. Here the question arises: where did Death see the deities? Death (Kaal) saw that once their karma was exhausted, the deities would come under his control — that is, once their merit is used up, they must take birth again in some other womb. Realizing this, the deities understood that their ritual works (karmakand) could no longer sustain them, and they became afraid. We have already said earlier that the gods enjoy their prosperity through the fruits of the offerings (homa) given to them by human beings, and that they are prepared to do anything to preserve that prosperity. Thus, even while understanding the truth, they are unable to follow it, for the sake of such fleeting happiness. Therefore the true Guru has told us —

_Tab to Omkar hi bhayo, Mayako sarno teen grahyo,
Omkar tab srishti nipaai, taki khabar kinahu nahi paai,
Aadya Purush te bhoole tabahi, Omkarku bhaage sabahi._
(Then it was Omkar alone that came to be, taking shelter under the three modes of Maya; Omkar then brought forth creation, but none has ever grasped its true nature; forgetting the Primordial Being at that very point, everyone has run after Omkar.)

Thus, falling under the delusion of momentary greed, the world has clung to Omkar and has forgotten the true Parbrahm. Like a blind man falling into a well, the world has fallen straight into the mouth of Death. All its cherished desires remain unfulfilled. Those who walk the path of the six schools of philosophy (khat darshan) do not realize that they are walking, of their own accord, straight into the mouth of Death — this is exactly like walking of one's own will straight into the mouth of a tiger. For this reason it is said in the Mahabharata —

_Chaturnam lokapalanam shukrasyatha brihaspateh,
Marutam vishwadevanam sadhyanamashwirapi. ||27||
Rudradityavasunam cha tathanyesham divaukasam,
Ete vai nirayastaat sthanasya paramatmanah. ||28|| (Shanti-198-5,6)_
(Varuna, Kubera, Indra, and Yamaraja — these four guardians of the world — and Shukra, Brihaspati, the Marut gods, the Vishvadevas, the Sadhyas, the Ashwini Kumaras, Rudra, the Adityas, the Vasus, and other deities — the abodes of all of these are, in comparison with the Supreme Abode of the Paramatma, like hell.)

For this very reason Jivanji Maharaj has said —

_Jahaan jahaan pandit paav dhare, tahaan tahaan Jamka vaas,
Sant paanv dhare Jivana, tahaan Sitapati avinash. ||73||_
(Wherever the pandit sets foot, there dwells Yama; wherever the saint sets foot, O Jivan, there is the imperishable Sitapati.)

That is, as long as the covering of Maya (illusion) that clings to the soul is not removed and its delusion is not destroyed, the soul cannot recognize Parbrahm. But as soon as the delusion is destroyed, it begins to experience Parbrahm directly. Regarding this, Kabirji says —

_Kabir gunakaar gun vistaryo, jab dhariyu e deh,
Bhagakaar tabe padhyo, sarvaale sahaj videh. ||53||_
(Kabir says: the gunas expanded through multiplication when this body was assumed; then division was learned; and in the sum total, effortlessly, one becomes bodiless.)

Kabirji has composed this couplet (sakhi) by bringing together the idea of division and multiplication. That is, our true Guru has performed a division of actions (karmas) and gunas — meaning Kabirji says that the gunas and karmas must be divided down, that they must gradually be reduced to zero. This is the state the soul must reach, where no number remains left over. It is for this reason that zero has been called the complete number — for when it is attained, all craving dissolves, and supreme bliss is attained, before which every worldly happiness appears puny.

In the end, whoever walks by relying upon the Guru's word incurs no karma, and no bondage remains for him. Thus, by the support of a single word, he can cross the ocean of worldly existence. This is the very matter being explained here: whoever wishes to take refuge in Shri Hari must give up all manner of crooked reasoning and argument, and hold fast to the path of good virtue (sadgun), so that, without wandering here and there elsewhere in the world, he may go straight to the Supreme Abode, into the refuge of Shri Hari.

Explaining the sense of this couplet, the revered Yadunath Maharaj has written: just as multiplication increases a number and division decreases it, so too the three gunas, when expanded, became the twenty-five categories (prakritis) of the five elements; and when the prakritis are drawn back in, only the five remain as five, and finally only the ego (aham) remains — and when that too is destroyed, only Ishwar remains alone.

When a body is assumed, the three gunas multiply together with the five elements, and so karma increases; but when the three-guna number belonging to Omkar is divided by Rarankar, the state of zero — the bodiless (videh) form — is attained easily and naturally, in a simple manner. Here, the "sum" of karma means, in the end — that is, at the conclusion of the process of multiplication, division, subtraction, and so on — the final outcome of karma. "Sum equals bodiless" means that at the end of the process of multiplication and division, the one who takes refuge in the true Guru attains the bodiless, effortless, zero-state of Parbrahm.

Narsinh Mehta was a devotee wholly devoted to Krishna alone. This was displeasing to the sannyasis (renunciate ascetics), and so seventeen sannyasis lodged a complaint against Narsinh Mehta before Ra' Mandalik, the king of the old monastery, saying that Narsinh Mehta was a hypocrite. They therefore had a garland placed upon the image of Damodardasji, saying that if God Himself gave that garland to Narsinh, only then would his devotion be judged true — otherwise he should be sentenced to death. At that time Narsinh Mehta sang the bhajans of the Harmala (garland cycle), in which he sharply rebuked the sannyasis and strongly criticized Omkar.

Raag Maru:

_Siddhi na hoy re Shripatne, siddhi na hoy re,
Vaishnav vina taryo na koy re. ||Tek||
Kahoji kayo sannyasi sharan ja paamyo, dandvesh jataadhari re,
Tamo Vaishnavoni ninda karo chho, bhoonda narakna adhikari re. ||1||
Tamari stri mare ne jyare khava tale, tyare bhagvaan pahero re,
Preet bhagati vairaag vina, fooko kaan ja beharo re. ||2||
Tamara Omkarnu karo re athanu, mahara Vrindavan chalo re,
Bhaje Narsaiyo mahelo dand kamandal, maahari poodhe taal vagado re. ||3||_
(Shripat shall never attain perfection — none has ever crossed over without being a Vaishnav. Tell me, which sannyasi, wearing the staff and matted locks, has ever attained true refuge? You slander the Vaishnavs, and so you deserve a wretched hell. When your wife dies and you have nothing to eat, only then do you put on the ochre robe; without true love, devotion, and renunciation, you merely blow into a deaf man's ear. Go pickle your Omkar — come instead to my Vrindavan! Narsaiya sings: give up your staff and water-pot, and play the cymbals with me instead.)

Meaning: Ascetics such as those called Shripat will never succeed in crossing the ocean of worldly existence, because no one can cross it without being a Vaishnav. Tell me yourselves — has anyone, merely by holding a staff and taking on the garb of a sannyasi or matted locks, ever managed to reach the refuge of God? You yourselves slander the Vaishnavs — you are so wicked that you deserve to attain a wretched hell. When your wife dies and, at that time of unease in the funeral rites, you feel restless, you put on ochre robes and become sannyasis; but without true love and renunciation for God, you merely make the sound of Omkar, blowing into the conch that produces the Omkar sound, blowing the mantra of Omkar into the ears of the deaf — that is, the uncomprehending. You urge people to practise the worship of Omkar, but such a useless Omkar, good for nothing, you may as well go on hoarding uselessly. If you truly wish your own good, give up ritualism (karmakand) and join me instead in devotion to Krishna of Vrindavan, and play the cymbals (kansi-manjira) while singing bhajans and kirtans.

Thus, in devotion to Vishnu (Vaishnav bhakti), devotees such as Narsinh Mehta have condemned Omkar as being like a thief posing as an honest merchant.

The saints split [the divine name] into its "ra" sound and its "m" sound, and gave the opinion that the "m" sound is in the form of maya (illusion), while the "ra" sound is the complete Brahman. Therefore the saints have embraced the "ra" sound. In the Kuvarpura Samagam it is written thus:

_Kabir nav lakh tara ugia, suraj koti hazar_
_Take timir bhange nahi, gor bina ghor andhar ||1||_
(Meaning: Even if nine hundred thousand stars were to rise, and thousands of millions of suns were to rise — that much light in the darkness of maya — still, for one who has not found a true Guru, the dense darkness of maya remains for him.)

Revered Yadunath Maharaj, in Note No. 50, "Pravas Sahayak" 6, page 166, has written a verse of salutation to every Guru in the Guru lineage, from Narayan down to the present day.

_Lakshminath samarambha nathyamun madhyamam_
_Asmadacharya paryantam vande guru paramparam ||1||_
(Meaning: Beginning with Narayan, the husband of Lakshmi, and including those who came in between such as Nath Muni and Yamunacharya, down to our own teachers to this day — I bow to every single Guru of this Guru lineage.)

This calculus of division and multiplication is understood only by one who has received the grace of Namdev and Kabir; only such a person can grasp this matter. Such compassion had indeed fallen upon Jivanji Maharaj, and so the true path was revealed to him. His worldly deeds and qualities had already been exhausted, and now, in surrender to the true Guru alone, he had only to recognize the Supreme Brahman. Further, through the meeting (samagam) that took place with the Guru, Jivanji Maharaj's inner eye opened, and he recognized the illusion (maya) of the world. That which he had had to wait for now stood before him of its own accord; what is difficult to attain had now become effortless. There was no need to wait any longer — Truth itself was now ready to come and sit before him. So on that day, that is, on the thirteenth of the bright half of Aso, Jivanji Maharaj went to meet Gopaldas and spent twenty-four hours in his company (samagam); through what unfolded there, the path of Truth was revealed to him. Therefore, two days later, that is, on the fifteenth of the bright half of Aso, Jivanji Maharaj, saying "Ramkabir," bowed to Gopaldas and confirmed him as his true Guru. Thus, on this day, the two of them were bound in the relationship of Guru and disciple. Jivanji Maharaj himself gives testimony to this.

_Sadguru das Gopalji, je Janakvansh avatar_
_Raghupati batayo Jivana, je Vrishabhan suta shanagar ||1||_
_Naam hamaro Jivana, kanabi kul avatar_
_Sai hamara Ramji, sadguru das Gopal ||2||_
_Kabir Ramkrishnathe ko bada, un guru seva kin_
_O to jagatke ishta the, pan guru aage aadhin ||3||_
(Meaning: Jivanji Maharaj says: My true Guru is the Vaishnav Gopaldas, who is of the Janak lineage. He has given me the vision of Raghupati [Ram], the beloved lord (Krishna) adorning Vrishabhan's daughter (Radhaji). My own name is Jivandas; I was born into the Kanbi [farming] caste. My chosen deity is Ramji, and my true Guru is the Vaishnav Gopaldasji. Addressing his Guru Gopaldasji, Jivanji Maharaj recites a couplet of Kabirji: that Ram and Krishna, though forms of the Supreme Brahman incarnate, still had to go to a Guru. Thus, whoever is born into this world, however great a ruler he may be, must still bow before a Guru. Ram and Krishna, though the chosen deities of the world, are themselves subordinate before the Guru. In this way, every person must take a Guru.)

Here, Jivanji Maharaj, having confirmed Gopaldasji as his Guru, gives the entire Guru lineage. Introducing the first Guru, he says that Gopaldasji is of the Janak lineage, and his original seat is Choranda. 1) His Guru is Dada Sukhji, who is known as being of the Pipa lineage and is a native of Shuklatirth. 2) His Guru is Gnaniji Maharaj. 3) Dwarkadasji 4) Narharidasji 5) Sari Ramdasji 6) Krishnadas Payahari 7) Karmachandji 8) Gemji 9) Joganandji 10) Anantanandji 11) Ramanandji 12) Radhavanandji 13) Hariananda 14) Devacharaj 15) Ramanidh 16) Ramanuj 17) Saraswati Bhatt 18) Lala Charaj 19) Acharya Jayamat 20) Ramanij 21) Kul Tarak 22) Ramayansh 23) Jayamatmuni 24) Ramamisar 25) Pundarik 26) Nathmuni 27) Mangalmuni 28) Bopadev Bhagavatlu 29) Shathgop 30) Sudhin 31) Muni Praj 32) Vishvaksen 33) Lakshmiji 34) Narayan.

Dada Sukhji:

In the Barot community, people are identified by lineages such as Janakvanshi, Pipavanshi, Hanumanvansh, and so on. Thus Gopaldasji was of the Janak lineage, and his Guru Dada Sukhji was of the Pipa lineage. In the Bhaktamal, a devotee named Lakhaji is called Vanaravanshi (of the monkey lineage). Of Nabha Swami too it is said that he was of the Dom lineage. People of castes such as Dom, Kalavant, Dhadhi, Bhaar, Kathak, and so on are of a kind that make their living through the art of singing.

Dr. Kantikumar Bhatt has called Gopaldas a Vanik (merchant), but this is a mistake — Gopaldasji was a Barot. Mr. Bhatt has written that because Gopaldas was as detached from the world as King Janak, he was therefore called Janakvanshi. But "Janakvanshi" and similar terms are actually sub-caste surnames used to identify one's own sub-division within the community. Gopaldasji's Guru, Dada Sukhji, was likewise of the Pipa lineage — so he too was not a Brahmin but a Barot. However, Mr. Bhatt has mistakenly described him as a Brahmin of Shinor.

Writing about Shukdev (Sukhji), Mr. Bhatt says that it is learned from the seat (gadi) of Gnaniji that he was a Brahmin of Shinor, and that he had paralysis in his left leg; he was brought to Gnaniji at Mota Sanja, and through Gnaniji's medicine the ailment was cured, after which he became Gnaniji's disciple. He had land and a house in Shinor, and lived by the priestly (yajaman) profession. It was Gnaniji who gave the Guru-mantra, the Name of Ram-Kabir. He used to recite the Bhagavat Katha at the Vyas temple near Karnali; the Maharajas of Vadodara had built a temple and rest-houses (dharmashalas) there. In one of his own couplets, Gnaniji mentions Shukdev's devotion to his Guru — that whoever serves the Guru truly, in thought, word, and deed, is saved; and to see the proof of this, he says, Shukdev is the witness:

_Manasa vacha karmana, jin kini gurusev_
_Gyani sohi ubra, sakshi suno Shukdev ||3||_
(Meaning: Those who have served their Guru with mind, speech, and action have been saved — hear that the witness to this is Shukdev.)

Shukdev could also be Vyas's son, but Mr. Bhatt has stated that this couplet refers to Sukhji. Whichever the case, Sukhji was Gnaniji's disciple, and he was not a Brahmin but a Barot; and people of the Barot community make their living through the priestly (yajaman) profession alone. Jivanji Maharaj's Guru, Gopaldas, was likewise a Barot — and moreover, in the ledger (chopdo) of the Barot who recorded Jivanji Maharaj's genealogy, a record of the generations from Jivanji Maharaj down to the present day has been entered. In their ledger, on page 412, it is written:

"Shri Jivanji Maharaj, of the Leva Patidar Amin family of village Karamsad, renounced his own house, mansion, and estate, and took up the path of teaching. He was born in his home village of Karamsad, Samvat 1649.

Shri Jivanji Maharaj manifested at the age of 11, in Samvat 1660, on Shravan Sud 8, in village Goriyad. At village Keslu, at the age of 16, spiritual discourse (gnan-goshti) took place with Mahant Gopaldasji of Choranda; village Choranda, Samvat 1683.

At village Choranda, Mahant Gopaldasji had the name of his disciple Jivanji Maharaj recorded; a gold armlet of one and a quarter tola, and 125 rupees and a shawl were given. After staying four years in village Choranda, he set out on pilgrimage to the Four Dhams, Samvat 1687, Ashadh Sud 10. He held a feast (bhandaro); a mare and 51 rupees and a pitambar (silk garment) were given. In village Mangleswar he performed six months of austerity (bhajan-bhakti). In Samvat 1717, Magsar Sud 2, the second day, he redeemed Bhoja Gujar. He held a feast; 51 rupees were placed on a copper vessel, and a silk abotiyu (upper cloth) was given. He stayed at village Mangleshwar, Samvat 1716, Jeth Sudi 2; village Dhanor, Samvat 1726, Bhadarva Sud 11.

Near village Kandari, in Puniyad country, Gujarat, Jivanji Maharaj held a feast, Samvat 1726; gold bangles, a dushala (shawl), and 125 rupees were given.

Ramanand, Anantanand, Gesji, Gnaniji, Gnandevji, Shamdevji, Ramdevji, Vasudevji, Narbheramji, Abheramji, Dayaramji, Rughnathdas Bhaibaba, Ramdas Hargovind Gopaldas, Gordhandas-Hansapura, Ramratandas, Sitaram, Ramkishandas Madhusudandas, Jugaldas, Jagdishdas.

"Bhagwandas Swami held feasts; Narsangdasji called nine assemblies, 1875; also Garibdas, Dharidas, Tulsidas."

The above is what is written in the genealogy ledger kept by the vahivancha (traditional genealogist-bard). The matter of Dada Sukhji calls for a great deal of further research. Haridas of Nadiad, in his Bhaktamal, Volume No. 44, page 31, writes in Kavit 1:

_Batak bijki mandmein, dekh bhaya man dhir_
_Dwarkadas updeshmein, sukhdata jetha bhaya ||4||_
(Meaning: Once, while urinating, Dwarkadasji, the Guru of Gnaniji, laughed on seeing a fig seed — the seed that gives rise to a tree as vast as a banyan — being swept away in the stream of urine. Seeing him laugh, Gnaniji also laughed; the Guru then asked why he had laughed. Gnaniji could give no answer, but later Kabirji explained: a tree as mighty as a banyan, which not even an elephant can uproot, has a seed that is carried helplessly away in urine — that is why the Guru had laughed. He who grasped this understanding, Gnaniji, became the disciple of the Guru Dwarkadas; and the great Dada Sukhji, also called Dada Jasvantji, became the one who received teaching from him and, in turn, bestowed it.)

The explanation of how "Sukhdata Jetha" comes to mean Dada Sukhji Jasvantji is found in the Kavit appearing in Handwritten Manuscript No. 37, page 137.

_Gyanike parmodhmein sukhdata Jasvantji bhaye_
_Take shikh Gopalji jan Jivankun updesh diyo ||5||_
(Meaning: The disciple who received Gnaniji's teaching was Sukhdata Jasvantji; his own disciple was Gopaldasji, who gave teaching to the devotee Jivanji.)

Thus, comparing the two, Sukhda Jasvantji comes to be Dada Jasvantji, also known as Dada Sukhji.

In "Nazar's Compilation" written by Nazar, Shamal Haribhai, Notebook No. 146, page 209, it is written:

"It appears that Jasvantji, the disciple of Gnaniji, must also have had the second name Dada Sakhaji (Sukhji). This seems so because in the earlier Kavit the name Jasvantji is found, and in the Guru lineage given in the Samagam, it is found as Dada Sakhji, of the Pipa lineage, resident of Shuklatirth. Considering everything, if each of these names belonged to a separate person, many years would have to have passed between them, and that does not seem possible; therefore it appears that all these names belong to one and the same person. This is also what Puniyad Swami Yadunathji holds, and on reflection it seems the same to me as well. Between Jivanji Maharaj and Gnaniji Maharaj, the one addressed as Gopaldas, Dada Sakhji, Dada Jasvant, and Sukhdata Jetha is one and the same person."

Gnaniji:

A whole essay could be written about Gnaniji, the Guru of Dada Sukhji, but let us look at it briefly. The true Guru Jivanji Maharaj has spoken about Gnaniji in Sakhi 129 of the Prabodh Ang:

_Gurjar khandma pragate, Gyani Gorakhnath_
_Das Kabire aayke, mastak dino hath ||6||_
(Meaning: Gorakhnath manifested in the region of Gujarat as Gnaniji; Das Kabir came and, placing his hand upon his head, bestowed grace and devotion upon him.)

_Gujaratmein Gyani bhaye, janat hai sab koy_
_Das Kabira aayke, darshan dina soy ||7||_
(Meaning: That a devotee such as Gnaniji appeared in Gujarat is a fact known to all; Das Kabirji came and blessed him with his darshan, making him fulfilled.)

In Handwritten Manuscript No. 31, page 205, the dialogue between Kabir and Gorakh is recorded; at its end, it is said that Gorakhnath, having lost, offered to Kabir the five symbols (matras) of Gorakhnath.

_Topi kopi kubadi jholi zhanda hath, kripa bhai Kabirki_
_Pancho matra sompi dinhi Gorakhnath ||8||_
(Meaning: The cap, the loincloth, the crutch-staff, the wallet, and the flag in hand — these the Gorakhpanthis keep. When Kabirji's grace descended, Gorakhnath handed over all five of these symbols to him.)

In a text composed under the title Garbhavali, Handwritten Register No. 208, from page 63, the discussion between Gorakh and Kabir is given. We have seen in the Kabir-Gorakh dialogue that Gorakh was defeated by Kabir. It is said that Gorakh, having attained 84 yogic powers (siddhis), came to conquer Kabir; sitting upon a trident, he began to say, "Debate with me." Then Kabirji held one end of a thread wound on a spinning spindle to the ground, flung the thread into the sky, and went and sat upon its far end, and told Gorakh, "Come and sit facing me." Then Gorakh, who had come to defeat him by the strength of his powers, admitted defeat and asked to be taught devotion (bhakti). Kabir then told Gorakh: "You have wasted your life on the path of yoga; but I will teach you devotion if you take another birth." It was for this reason that Gorakh came, taking birth as Gnaniji. In the text Garbhavali, the plea that Gorakh made to Kabir is described.

Gorakh Uvach (Gorakh said):

_Suno Swami garabh bandhana, kese hansa hoye chhutana_
_Kese mite jatharki trasa, so Saheb kaho ham pasa ||9||_
(Meaning: Gorakh said, "O Swami, listen — how does the swan-soul bound in the womb become free, and how does the torment of the womb-fire end? Tell me this, O Master.")

[Sakhi]

_Nij gyan samjhavahu, dusar janam tumhar_
_So Jesalmer janamiya, Bhathi kul Rajput_
_Gurjar dhar (desh) pavan kiyo, so Gyani gun avdhut_

(Meaning: The true Guru Kabir said: Now I tell you the secret — go and take birth in the land of Murdhar. There, in Jaisalmer within Murdhar, take incarnation in a Bhati household. Your name will be Gyani (Gnaniji), and you shall take the teaching of the Guru Khojiji. Afterward, come into Gujarat, and dwell in the fine, level land of the Kanam region, wherever your abode is to be. And I myself, in this very body of Kabir, will instruct you, and your entire Gorakh-panth will be shaken and drawn away toward devotion; and the path (bhekh) of devotion that you take up there will spread through the world. I will bring about the deliverance of your soul — but right now you are practising the discipline of celibacy, preserving the seed, and, seeing the womb, you are greatly afraid, and so you will come into the womb. Thinking of going by your path, that is, Kabirji's path, this thought arose in Gorakh's mind: "Let me take a body and be born in Sindh, taking incarnation in a Kshatriya household, and by various means bring about my own deliverance."

Sakhi: Gorakh began to say: "True Guru, listen — I shall indeed take birth, but afterward, how will I meet you? Explain this to me, Guru."

With joined hands Gorakh said: "O all-knowing Swami, listen — keep me in your refuge, and give me the teaching of your own knowledge."

Kabirji's word — Kabir said: "When Khojiji laughs while urinating, you too will burst out laughing without restraint. Then Khojiji will be puzzled: 'I laughed, but why did you laugh? Tell me the reason for my laughter.' And so, when you set out to seek me in order to find that reason, I will grant you my darshan, and the doubt that Khojiji had raised for you will be resolved, and your deliverance will come about easily."

Seeing the seed of a banyan's fig swept away in urine, Khojiji's mind was struck with wonder; and when the true Guru Kabir was met, the resolution came to the doubt about the question Gnaniji had asked — that as long as the seed remained attached to the tree it was safe, but once separated from the tree it is swept away in filth and urine. In the same way, the soul (jiva) remains safe as long as it is attached to the feet of the Lord; but turning away from God, it drifts about in the ocean of worldly existence, in the filth of the womb. The tree is contained within the seed, and the seed is contained within the tree; in the same way, the world is interwoven with God, and God with the world.

Kabir then said: "Gorakh, heed what I say — I will explain my own true knowledge to you in your next incarnation."

Thus this Gorakh was born in Jaisalmer, in a Bhatia Rajput family, and this Gnaniji, possessed of the qualities of an avadhut, sanctified the region of Gujarat.)

The devotional hymn (pad) written about Gorakhnath by Dayaldas, the Udabhagat of Vayadapol, introduces us to Gnaniji. Nazar has translated the verses of that hymn relating to Gnaniji, as follows:

"Gorakhji sought teaching from Kabir; Gorakhji shed his old garb. Gorakh was born in the land of Murdhar, where he was named Chatursangh. At the age of 11, Chatur Sangh was to be given the royal coronation-mark (rajtilak), but Chatur Sangh thought, 'I have taken this body for devotion; if I take up rule I shall fall into the snare of maya, and shall have to face a dark end.' So, at midnight, he left that place and, coming into Gujarat, at the pond-bank of village Sokhda, took up the garb of an ascetic and rested there. Each day a Brahmin woman used to bring him food; that woman's son died, and Chatursangh brought the son back to life. After this, Chatursangh left Sokhda (the name of the next village is worn away and cannot be read) .... and went and met Dwarkadasji. He showed Chatursangh the Name of Ram. Once, Dwarkadas laughed, and so Chatursangh laughed too. Chatursangh set out to discover the reason for the laughter. Meditating on the island (bet) of the Reva [Narmada], he performed austerities for seven days; one morning, at sunrise, Kabirji, after cleaning his teeth with a twig, planted the split twig, and it grew into a banyan tree. Chatursangh left off his meditation and bowed at his feet; Kabirji then revealed the secret to him, and Chatursangh went to Dwarkadas and said:"

_Dayala vari utarat behe gayo, vatko bij chanik_
_Tab gurudev yun boliya, baat kahi te nik ||10||_
(Meaning: Dayaldas writes: "While urinating, the seed of the little banyan fig was swept away — that is why you laughed." Then the Guru said, "Now you have spoken the truth correctly.")

"After this, both Chatursangh and Dwarkadasji came to Kabirji, and Kabirji explained to both of them the teaching of the Agam-panth."
